I didn’t have time Friday so thought I’d do a quick post on the University of Michigan consumer sentiment report as it had some interesting items.

The preliminary read of for September released Friday fell 7.5% to 47.8, the second consecutive monthly decline below every estimate in a Bloomberg survey of economists (51.0 expected), down from August’s 51.7, and just 3 points above the all-time low from May. The University of Michigan said its consumer sentiment index slumped to 47.8 in September after tumbling to 51.7 in August. Economists had expected the index to edge down to 51.0. # US Consumer Sentiment Falls as Inflation Expectations Rise

The University of Michigan’s consumer sentiment index fell to 47.8 in early September 2026, down for a second consecutive month and well below market expectations of 51.0, according to the preliminary estimate.

It was the weakest reading since May’s record low.

results.title: U.S. Consumer Sentiment Unexpectedly Deteriorates, Inflation Expectations Rise as Dollar Trades Near Lows

results.content:
The University of Michigan’s Index of Consumer Sentiment fell to 47.8 in the preliminary September reading from 51.7 in August, a 7.5% monthly drop that leaves it the second-lowest print in the survey’s history and 13.2% below where it stood a year ago.

The damage was almost entirely forward-looking. The Index of Consumer Expectations plunged 11.1% to 45.8, while Current Economic Conditions slipped just 1.9% to 50.9.
